olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Triangle $ABC$ is inscribed in circle $\omega$. A circle $\Gamma$ passes through $A$ and meets segment $BC$ at two distinct points $D$ and $E$ such that
$$BD<CD<CE.$$
The circumcircles of triangles $ABD$ and $ACE$ meet line $BC$ again at points $X$ and $Y$, respectively. Prove that the lines $AX,AY,$ and the tangent to $\Gamma$ at $A$ are concurrent.
figure_description: Triangle with an auxiliary circle through a vertex intersecting the opposite side.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Let
$$a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots$$
be an infinite sequence of positive integers. Suppose there is an integer $N>1$ such that, for each positive integer $n$, the number of indices $i$ with
$$a_i=n$$
is finite and less than $N$. Prove that there exists a nonempty finite set $S$ of positive integers such that
$$
\sum_{i\in S}\frac1{a_i}=1.
$$

In the game of Hyper Knight, Chuck and Sandra play on a chessboard with finitely many rows and columns. Chuck places a knight on a starting square of his choice, and Sandra then chooses an ending square. Chuck can move the knight any number of times, but is not allowed to revisit a square he has already visited. Sandra wins if Chuck can reach the ending square; otherwise, Chuck wins.

Find all pairs $(m,n)$ of positive integers such that Sandra has a winning strategy on every $m\times n$ chessboard.
figure_description: Knight-move reachability game on finite chessboards.

statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. The numbers
$$k_1,k_2,\ldots,k_n$$
are positive integers not exceeding $n$ such that
$$k_i+k_j>n$$
for all
$$1\le i<j\le n.$$
Prove that
$$
\frac1{k_1}+ rac1{k_2}+\cdots+\frac1{k_n}
\le
2.
$$

Let $ABCDE$ be a convex pentagon such that
$$AB=BC=CD=DE.$$
Suppose that there is a point $P$ inside the pentagon such that
$$PA=PE$$
and
$$PB=PD.$$
Prove that line $PC$ bisects at least one of the angles
$$\angle BCD\quad\text{or}\quad\angle AP E.$$
figure_description: Convex pentagon with equal consecutive sides and interior-point symmetry conditions.

statement:
For each finite set $A$ of positive integers, let
$$\sigma(A)$$
denote the sum of the elements of $A$. Let $X$ be a set of $2015$ distinct positive integers. Prove that there exist two nonempty disjoint subsets $A$ and $B$ of $X$ such that
$$
\sigma(A)
\mid
\sigma(B).
$$
